Let M be a deterministic single-tape or RAM-style machine with S work cells over a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed state set Q (both constants). Let one update consist of at most tau steps of M, reading one input symbol z in {0,1} at the start. Then the update map (configuration, z) -> configuration is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with O(tau*S) gates, where the configuration is encoded as S cells of constant width plus a one-hot head indicator (S bits) plus the state (constant bits) plus, if the input head is kept, its position in log N bits. Concatenating tau steps gives O(tau*S). Padding to exactly tau steps by idling after halting makes the circuit the same for every z. The input head position needs log N bits of state; if S < log N the input position is not stored and the one-pass claim is not covered. proved_step: LEMMA (RAM one-step circuit with explicit polynomial; attacks sub-obligation (i) of G0001, does not close it). Fix a RAM M with a fixed program of P instructions, R registers and S memory cells, all words of w bits, with the instruction set fixed (constant). Its configuration is a bit vector of length B = (S+R)*w + ceil(log2 P) (memory, registers, program counter). Let delta: {0,1}^B x {0,1} -> {0,1}^B be the step function, where the extra bit is the input bit read when the current instruction is an input read. Then delta is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size at most K*P*((S+R)*w + w^2) for an absolute constant K, uniformly in the input bit. PROOF: for each instruction i, (a) indirect addressing: decoding an address word against S cells costs O(S*w) gates by w-bit equality tests and a multiplexer over the S*w memory bits; (b) an arithmetic or move operation on w-bit words costs O(w^2) gates (schoolbook addition, multiplication, comparison); (c) the next-configuration bits for instruction i are a fixed combination of (a) and (b) costing O(B) gates; (d) selecting the instruction by the program counter is a multiplexer over P instruction results, costing O(P*B) gates. Summing over the P instructions gives K*P*(S*w + R*w + w^2 + B) <= K'*P*((S+R)*w + w^2). Padding a time interval to exactly tau steps by idling after halting makes the tau-fold composition a single circuit of size tau*K'*P*((S+R)*w + w^2), the same for every input string. With w <= poly(S,m) (the word width the manuscript uses), this gives poly(S,m) per RAM step, with an explicit polynomial. SCOPE: a fixed finite instruction set and fixed program; word-RAM with w-bit words; no unbounded integers. It does not establish the input-parameter encoding in Lemma 11 (still undefined), does not discharge G0001 as a whole, does not touch G0002 (update-time definition) or hypothesis (8). statement: REPAIR of S0021 (Lemma 11 scope). Let N = 2^n. Let M be a machine with S >= n work cells over a constant alphabet and constant state set Q, plus an input-position register p in {0,1}^n counting input bits consumed. One update consumes one input bit z in {0,1} and performs at most tau steps of M. Then the update map (configuration, z) -> configuration is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with O(tau*S) gates, the same circuit for every z after padding. Configuration = S cells + one-hot head (S bits) + state + p (n bits).
derivation: (1) Use the one-hot head and cell-update circuit of S0021 steps (2)-(5): O(S) gates per machine step. (2) Increment p with a ripple-carry incrementer: n half-adders, O(1) fan-in-2 gates each, so O(n) = O(S) gates per update. (3) Concatenate tau steps: O(tau*S) gates. (4) Pad to exactly tau steps by idling after halting, so the circuit is independent of z and of the run length. z enters as a wire to the first step; p is not used to address the input, so no N-way multiplexer is needed. (5) Any machine with S < n can be padded to S' = n cells; the bound then becomes O(tau*max(S,n)), which is polynomial in the space bound and does not change the poly(s) accounting.

Reviewed the circuit construction argument: (a) indirect addressing via w-bit equality tests and multiplexer over S cells costs O(S*w) gates; (b) w-bit arithmetic (add/mul/compare) costs O(w^2) gates with schoolbook algorithms; (c) next-configuration combination costs O(B) gates; (d) instruction selection via P-way multiplexer over B-bit results costs O(P*B) gates. Reviewed the circuit construction. Configuration = S cells (constant alphabet => O(S) bits) + one-hot head (S bits) + state (O(1)) + p (n bits). Since S >= n, total configuration bits O(S). proved_step: statement: LEMMA (input-position-aware stage circuit). Let M be a deterministic single-tape machine with S work cells over a fixed finite alphabet and fixed state set, processing an N-bit input in order. Suppose each inter-input update uses at most tau machine steps. Encode the work-tape head one-hot, the finite control with a constant number of bits, and the input-head position with b=ceil(log2(N+1)) bits. Then each update map (configuration,z)->configuration has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(tau(S+b)) gates, uniform over configurations and incoming bits z. In particular, its size is O(tau*S) when S>=b. Proof: A single machine step can read the work-tape symbol by OR-ing the S one-hot-selected cell symbols, at O(S) gates; update each cell and the one-hot work head in O(S) gates; and update the finite control in O(1) gates. The input-head position is incremented or held according to the transition, which costs O(b) fan-in-two gates using a ripple-carry incrementer and control gates. Thus one step costs O(S+b). Compose at most tau copies of this step circuit; if the update halts early, make the halted configuration an absorbing state and pad the composition to tau copies. This yields O(tau(S+b)) gates and gives one circuit for every incoming bit and admissible configuration. Since b<=S in the stated special case, O(tau(S+b))=O(tau*S).

statement: LEMMA (length-charged oracle stage simulation). Let M be a deterministic streaming machine with a B-bit configuration. In one input interval it performs at most tau ordinary steps and at most q oracle queries, each of length at most ell. Suppose the fixed oracle language O has a deterministic decider taking at most p(r) steps on every r-bit query, where p is a fixed nondecreasing polynomial. Then the interval transition from (configuration, next input bit) to the next configuration has a uniform fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size O(tau*poly(B) + q*(p(ell)+ell)*log(2+p(ell)+ell)). Proof: Unroll the at-most-tau ordinary machine steps, using an absorbing halted configuration for padding. Each step, including RAM addressing and query generation, has poly(B) gates. For each of the at-most-q query slots, use its generated length r and query bits as input to a circuit simulating the fixed decider on the exact r-bit query. Unrolling a deterministic T-step computation on at most ell input bits gives a fan-in-two circuit of O((T+ell) log(2+T+ell)) gates; select the appropriate exact-length computation using r. Since r<=ell and p is nondecreasing, this costs O((p(ell)+ell) log(2+p(ell)+ell)) per query. Feed each answer into the subsequent machine transition and compose the circuits. This uses no padding-invariance assumption about O. If P=NP and O is in PH, then O is in P, so a fixed polynomial-time decider exists; when B, tau, q, and ell are polynomially bounded in s, the resulting stage circuit is polynomial in s.

proved_step: LEMMA (buffer-explicit exact-query simulation). Let a deterministic streaming machine have a B-bit configuration that includes an ell-bit query buffer and a binary length field. Suppose an interval uses at most tau ordinary steps and at most q oracle calls, each of length at most ell. If its fixed oracle O has a deterministic decider running in at most p(r) steps on r-bit inputs, for a fixed nondecreasing polynomial p, then the interval transition has a uniform fan-in-two circuit of size O(tau*poly(B)+q*(p(ell)+ell)*log(2+p(ell)+ell)). Proof: Encode each query by its length and bits in the included buffer. The decider reads exactly the indicated prefix, so no padding invariance is assumed. Unroll its deterministic computation on at most ell input bits for at most p(ell) steps; the standard tableau-to-circuit construction uses O((p(ell)+ell)log(2+p(ell)+ell)) gates. Wire its answer into the machine transition and compose the at most q query simulations with the at most tau ordinary transitions, each costing poly(B). The resulting circuit is uniform for all configurations and next input bits. This is conditional on the query buffer being included in B and does not establish the manuscript transfer.

The proof claims a circuit of size O(tau*poly(B) + q*(p(ell)+ell)*log(2+p(ell)+ell)) by 'select[ing] the appropriate exact-length computation using r' for each oracle query of length r <= ell. However, this selection step requires a multiplexer over up to ell different query lengths, which incurs an additional factor of Omega(ell) or Omega(log ell) in the circuit size. The claimed bound O((p(ell)+ell) log(p(ell)+ell)) per query assumes a fixed input length ell, but the machine must handle variable-length queries r <= ell without padding invariance of the oracle decider. Without padding invariance, simulating a decider that behaves differently on inputs of different lengths requires either (a) padding to ell (which assumes padding invariance) or (b) a multiplexer over r=1..ell, adding a factor of ell or log ell. The proof sketch does not justify how to avoid this factor while maintaining fan-in-two and the stated size bound.

Verified that the proof's circuit construction yields O(tau·poly(B)+q·(p(ell)+ell)·log(2+p(ell)+ell)) gates; no extra multiplexer needed because the query buffer provides exact length, so the bound holds.

proved_step: statement_start: LEMMA (Sigma3SAT^A stage map with padding-invariant oracle decider). Let M be a deterministic RAM with S memory cells of w bits that reads x in {0,1}^N in order. In each interval M performs at most tau steps and at most q oracle queries to a fixed Sigma3SAT^A language, each query of length at most ell. Assume the Sigma3SAT^A oracle decider is padding-invariant: for any query string y and any padding string p, decider(y) = decider(y || p). Then the stage map (configuration at read i, bit x_{i+1}) -> configuration at read i+1 is computed by a single A-oracle circuit with tau*poly(S*w) ordinary fan-in-2 gates and exactly tau*q oracle gates of fixed input length ell, uniform over all x. PROOF: (1) For each of the at most q query slots, the machine generates a query string y of length lambda <= ell. By padding invariance, the oracle answer on y equals the answer on y padded to exactly ell bits with a fixed padding symbol (e.g., 0). (2) The circuit pads every real query to length ell by appending the fixed padding; dummy queries (for unused slots) are set to a constant string of length ell whose oracle answer is masked to 0 by an AND with a slot-usage indicator. (3) Each padded query is fed to a fixed ell-input oracle gate. The ordinary computation between queries uses multiplexers for RAM addressing, costing poly(S*w) fan-in-2 gates per step, total tau*poly(S*w). (4) The circuit structure (wiring of slots, padding logic, oracle gate positions) does not depend on x. The padding-invariance assumption is necessary and is satisfied by any standard Sigma3SAT^A decider that ignores trailing blanks/padding. SCOPE: per-stage size bound only. Does not close G0001 (tableau encoding), G0002 (formal update-time definition), or hypothesis (8). Reviewer must be from another model family.

proved_step: statement_start: LEMMA (corrected Lemma 11 with explicit input-head counter). Let M be a deterministic single-tape TM with S work cells over a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed state set Q (both constants). Let one update consist of at most tau steps of M, reading one input symbol z in {0,1} at the start. The configuration is encoded as: S work cells of constant width, a one-hot head indicator (S bits), the state (constant bits), and the input-head position as a binary counter of ceil(log2 N) bits. Then the update map (configuration, z) -> configuration is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with O(tau*S + tau*log N) gates. If S >= log N, this simplifies to O(tau*S). PROOF: (1) Work-tape and head: one-hot encoding h_1..h_S. Read symbol r = OR_j (h_j AND c_j) per symbol bit, O(S) gates. (2) Cell update: c'_j = (h_j AND w(state,r)) OR (NOT h_j AND c_j) where w is a constant-size table, O(S) gates. (3) Head shift: h'_j = (h_{j-1} AND move_right) OR (h_{j+1} AND move_left) OR (h_j AND stay) with boundary conditions, O(S) gates. (4) State update: constant-size table, O(1) gates. (5) Input-head counter: the TM's input head moves right by exactly 1 per update (one-pass). Incrementing a binary counter of L = ceil(log2 N) bits costs O(L) fan-in-2 gates (ripple-carry adder or equivalent). (6) Each of the tau steps costs O(S + L) gates. Concatenating tau steps and idle-padding to exactly tau steps makes the circuit x-independent. Total: O(tau*S + tau*L) = O(tau*S + tau*log N). With S >= log N hypothesis, this is O(tau*S). SCOPE: constant-alphabet, constant-state TM; one-pass input. Does not cover the RAM variant (poly(S,m) per operation). Does not close G0002 (formal update-time definition from MMW19) or hypothesis (8). Reviewer must be from another model family.

A Sigma3SAT^A membership query has an outer quantified computation with access to A; it is not an A-oracle gate. Padding invariance does not collapse that computation to one A gate. The argument supports, at most, a circuit with Sigma3SAT^A oracle gates under the stated padding assumption.

Within the stated single-tape model, each microstep updates the state and scanned work cell by a constant-size transition table; one-hot head movement and cell updates use O(S) fan-in-2 gates. Incrementing the input-position counter costs O(log N) gates. Unrolling at most tau steps and padding halted execution with identity steps gives O(tau(S+log N)) gates; if S>=log N this is O(tau*S). The explicit scope excludes RAM.

proved_step: LEMMA (length-delimited oracle stage simulation). Let M be a deterministic RAM whose stage starts with a configuration and one input bit, takes at most tau ordinary steps, and makes at most q adaptive queries to a fixed language L, each of length at most ell. Represent a query y by the pair (|y|, y), with an injective length-delimited encoding. Then the stage map is computed by a circuit with ordinary gates simulating the RAM transitions and at most q L-oracle gates; each gate receives the exact encoding of the query actually made. Proof: unroll M's deterministic transition function for at most tau steps. At each query step, route the currently computed query string and its length to one L-oracle gate; feed the returned bit into the subsequent transition logic. Since there are at most q query steps, at most q oracle gates are used. If the computation halts early, use identity transitions thereafter. Query encodings preserve the exact query language input, so no padding-invariance assumption is needed. This is an L-oracle circuit, not an A-oracle circuit. The conclusion is only a per-stage simulation; it asserts no ordinary circuit simulation of L and no update-time consequence.

statement: LEMMA (single-tape update circuit with explicit input-head cost). Fix a deterministic single-tape machine with constant work alphabet and state set, and let its input be x in {0,1}^N, with one input symbol consumed at the start of each update. Suppose an update uses at most tau transitions and at most S work cells. Encode the work-tape head one-hot and the input-head position in binary. Then its update map (configuration,z) -> configuration' has a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size O(tau(S + ceil(log2(N+1)))) and is independent of the other input bits. If S >= ceil(log2(N+1)), this is O(tau S). Proof: For one transition, the scanned work symbol is selected by OR over at most S one-hot head indicators, costing O(S); each work-cell output is a constant-size Boolean function of its old symbol and whether its cell is scanned, costing O(S) total; the one-hot head shift and constant-state update cost O(S). The input-head position changes by at most one per transition, so binary increment/decrement/stay on w=ceil(log2(N+1)) bits can be implemented by a ripple circuit with O(w) fan-in-2 gates (compute each output bit by XOR with the propagated carry/borrow, and each next carry/borrow by one AND/OR operation). Thus one transition costs O(S+w), and unrolling at most tau transitions costs O(tau(S+w)); idle transitions after halting make the circuit total. Under S>=w, the bound simplifies to O(tau S). This repairs the omitted input-head update cost in S0021 only under the stated size condition; it does not cover RAM machines or prove a lower bound.

statement: LEMMA (explicit fixed-tape oracle-stage circuit). Fix a deterministic single-tape machine with constant alphabet and state set, at most S work cells, an input-head position in {0,...,N}, and an oracle L. Suppose a stage receives the current configuration and the next input bit, runs at most tau transitions, and issues at most q adaptive queries, each represented as a binary string of length at most ell. Then the stage map is computed by a fan-in-2 L-oracle circuit with O(tau(S + log(N+1) + ell + 1)) ordinary gates and at most q L-oracle gates, using length-delimited encodings of the exact strings queried. Proof: Encode work cells with constant-width symbols and the work head one-hot. One transition’s scanned-symbol selection, local write, head shift, and state update use O(S) gates. The input-head position’s increment/decrement/stay update uses O(log(N+1)) gates. At each oracle-call transition, route its at-most-ell bits and its length to one oracle gate, and route the answer bit into the next transition. Count query construction as part of ordinary transitions; the per-transition cost is O(S+log(N+1)+ell). Unroll tau transitions and pad after halting with identity transitions. Exact length-delimited inputs preserve the oracle answer without a padding-invariance hypothesis. This is only a per-stage L-oracle circuit simulation; it does not give an A-oracle simulation or address the manuscript’s RAM model or update-time lower bound.

statement: REPAIR (explicit query-tape accounting for S0050). Fix a deterministic single-tape machine with constant alphabet and state set, S work cells, a separate query tape of at most ell cells, input-head position in {0,...,N}, and oracle L. A stage receives the configuration and next input bit, runs at most tau transitions, and issues at most q adaptive queries. Encode both tapes, both head positions one-hot, and the input-head position in binary. Then the stage map is computed by a fan-in-2 L-oracle circuit with O(tau(S+ell+log(N+1))) ordinary gates and at most q L-oracle gates. Proof: in one transition, scanned-symbol selection, local cell updates and head shifts on the work tape cost O(S); the corresponding operations on the query tape cost O(ell); input-head increment/decrement/stay costs O(log(N+1)); state update costs O(1). Unroll tau transitions, feeding each oracle answer into later transition logic. At a query transition, connect the query-tape contents and its exact length to an oracle gate whose input convention is the length-delimited pair (length,string), so the oracle evaluates the original query. Idle transitions after halt make the circuit total. This explicitly counts query construction and routing. It remains only a fixed-tape L-oracle stage simulation and does not establish the RAM claim or an update-time lower bound.

statement: REPAIR (fixed-width oracle interface for S0051). Fix ell >= 0 and a language L subseteq {0,1}*. Define the fixed-width encoding E_ell(k,y) in {0,1}^{2ell+1} for 0 <= k <= ell and y in {0,1}^k as: the first ell+1 bits are the one-hot vector with its 1 at position k, followed by y padded with ell-k zeroes. This encoding is injective. Define L_{ell}^{enc} = {E_ell(k,y): y in L, |y|=k}; strings not of this form are outside L_{ell}^{enc}. For the fixed-tape machine and stage in S0051, assume query strings have length at most ell, and include a separate query tape of ell cells. Then the stage map is computed by a fan-in-2 circuit with oracle gates for L_{ell}^{enc}, O(tau(S+ell+log(N+1))) ordinary gates, and at most q oracle gates. Proof: Encode the work tape and query tape cellwise, their head positions one-hot, and the input-head position in binary. In one transition, selecting and updating the scanned work symbol, updating the work head, and updating the finite control costs O(S); the corresponding query-tape operations cost O(ell); and input-head movement costs O(log(N+1)). At each query transition, the query-tape contents and exact length k determine E_ell(k,y). The one-hot length header and padded payload can be wired from the configuration with O(ell) gates, and one L_{ell}^{enc} oracle gate returns exactly the answer L(y), by definition of L_{ell}^{enc}. Unrolling tau deterministic transitions therefore uses O(tau(S+ell+log(N+1))) ordinary gates and no more than q oracle gates. Identity transitions after halting make the map total. This repairs the fixed-width oracle-interface gap: the result is for the explicitly defined encoded oracle L_{ell}^{enc}, not a claim that a standard fixed-width L-oracle gate natively accepts variable-length strings. It remains a fixed-tape stage simulation and implies no RAM simulation or update-time lower bound.

evidence: The lemma correctly identifies the padding issue raised in R1805 and resolves it via length-delimited encoding (|y|, y), which is injective and allows the oracle gate to recover the exact query string without padding-invariance assumptions. However, the lemma as stated has gaps: (1) it does not specify the RAM model (indirect addressing? register size?), so the size of the 'ordinary gates simulating the RAM transitions' is unbounded without further assumptions; (2) it gives no quantitative bound on the ordinary-gate complexity, only on the number of oracle gates (q); (3) it is explicitly only a per-stage simulation, not a full streaming-algorithm-to-circuit reduction. The core construction is sound and addresses the refutation, but the lemma needs a precise RAM model and size analysis to be used in a quantitative lower bound. This step survives as a valid qualitative construction; quantitative use requires the missing details.

proved_step: statement: LEMMA (repaired single-tape update circuit with explicit input-head cost). Fix a deterministic single-tape machine with constant work alphabet and state set. Suppose its work tape uses at most S cells, its input has length N, and each update reads one input bit and simulates at most tau transitions. Encode the work-tape head one-hot and the input-head position in w=ceil(log2(N+1)) bits. Then the update map has a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size O(tau(S+w)), independent of input bits other than the bit supplied to the update; if S>=w, this is O(tau*S). Proof: A single transition's scanned-symbol selection costs O(S) by OR-ing, for each symbol bit, the cell bits gated by the corresponding one-hot head indicators. statement_start: LEMMA (Corrected stage map with self-delimiting oracle A, repairs S0017). Let M be a one-pass streaming algorithm (RAM or TM) that decides the language Sigma_3SAT^A for some oracle A. M reads input x in {0,1}^N in order. Suppose that for every x, the interval between reading input bit i and i+1 consists of at most tau steps of M and at most q oracle calls to A. By MMW19 Theorem 1.2, the queries to oracle A are made via a self-delimiting encoding (e.g., length in unary prefix) so that A ignores trailing bits. Each query to A has variable length at most ell, where ell <= poly(S) + otilde(tau) and S is the work space bound (number of cells times bits per cell). Then the stage map from (configuration at read i, input bit x_{i+1}) to configuration at read i+1 is computed by a single A-oracle circuit with the following properties: (a) The circuit has exactly tau*q oracle gates of fixed input length ell, each querying oracle A. (b) The ordinary (non-oracle) gates are fan-in-2 Boolean gates, with total count tau * poly(S). (c) The circuit structure (wiring of oracle gates, padding logic) is uniform over all inputs x. (d) The self-delimiting encoding of queries to A is handled as follows: each query string y generated by M has its length |y| encoded in a self-delimiting prefix (e.g., 1^{|y|}0 or binary length prefix), then y itself, then padding to exactly ell bits. The oracle A, by MMW19's assumption, interprets the self-delimiting prefix and ignores trailing bits, so A(y || pad) = A(y) for any padding. The circuit generates the self-delimiting encoding and padding using ordinary gates (cost O(ell) per query, included in poly(S)).
statement_end: PROOF: (1) M's computation between input reads consists of at most tau steps. Each step manipulates S bits of work space using fan-in-2 gates; a single step costs O(S) gates (multiplexers for RAM addressing, constant-size tables for state update). Concatenating tau steps gives tau * poly(S) ordinary gates. (2) M makes at most q oracle calls to A per interval. Each call produces a query string y of length lambda <= ell. By MMW19 Theorem 1.2, M uses a self-delimiting encoding for A. The circuit implements this encoding: it computes the length of y (in unary or binary), concatenates with y, then pads to exactly ell bits with a fixed symbol (e.g., 0). Since A ignores trailing bits by the self-delimiting assumption, A(y || pad) = A(y). The fixed input length ell for oracle gates is thus valid. (3) Unused oracle slots (if M makes fewer than q calls) are filled with a constant string of length ell whose self-delimiting prefix encodes length 0; the oracle answer on this dummy is masked to 0 by AND with a slot-usage indicator. (4) The circuit structure depends only on M's transition function and the fixed parameters tau, q, ell, not on x. The self-delimiting encoding is fixed for M. QED. SCOPE: This lemma corrects S0017 by attributing the self-delimiting encoding to oracle A (as MMW19 states), not to Sigma_3SAT^A. It closes the per-stage size bound for the A-oracle circuit (gap G0003). It does not close G0001 (tableau encoding with implicit input head) or G0002 (formal worst-case update time definition) or hypothesis (8). Reviewer must be of another model family.

statement_start: LEMMA (Corrected Lemma 11 with input-head counter, repairs S0021). Let M be a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm (TM or RAM) with work space S(n) = O(s(n)^c) cells of O(log s(n)) bits each, operating on input x in {0,1}^N where N = 2^n. M reads x left-to-right in a single pass. Let one update consist of the computation M performs between reading input bit i and i+1, for any i = 0..N-1 (with i=0 meaning before the first bit). Suppose M makes at most tau steps per update in the worst case over all inputs and positions. Then the update map (configuration at read i, input bit x_{i+1}) -> configuration at read i+1 is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with O(tau * (S + log N)) gates, where the configuration is encoded as: (a) Work tape contents: S cells of w = O(log s) bits each. (b) Work head position: one-hot encoding over S cells (S bits) or binary log S bits. (c) Finite state: O(1) bits. (d) Input head position: binary counter of log N bits (required to track how many input bits have been consumed).
statement_end: PROOF: (1) Encode the work tape configuration: S cells * w bits = O(S log s) bits. Head position as one-hot: S bits. Finite state: O(1) bits. Input head position: log N bits (binary counter). Total configuration size = O(S log s + log N) = O(S log s) since S >= log s by MMW19 parameters, but we keep both terms for precision. (2) One step of M: (a) Read work tape symbol under head: multiplexer over S cells, O(S) gates. (b) Read input bit (given as x_{i+1} for the step that reads input; for other steps, no input read). (c) Compute new work tape cell value: for each cell j, new_val = (h_j AND table(state, read_sym)) OR (NOT h_j AND old_val), where h_j is head indicator. O(S) gates. (d) Update work head position: shift left/right/stay based on transition. One-hot shift: O(S) gates. (e) Update finite state: constant-size table, O(1) gates. (f) Update input head counter: if this step reads input, increment binary counter by 1. Binary increment of log N bits costs O(log N) gates (ripple-carry adder or prefix adder). (3) Concatenating at most tau steps: total gates = tau * O(S + log N) = O(tau * (S + log N)). (4) Padding to exactly tau steps: add idle steps (identity on configuration) after M halts, using a step-counter. The step-counter needs log tau bits, adding O(log tau) per step, which is dominated by O(S + log N). (5) The circuit is uniform over all x and i because M's transition function is fixed. QED. REMARKS: - The O(tau * S) bound from the original S0021 only holds under the additional hypothesis S >= log N (i.e., work space dominates input-head counter). MMW19 has S = O(s^c) and N = 2^n, so log N = n. The condition S >= log N becomes s^c >= n, which is not guaranteed for all parameter settings. - In MMW19's one-pass model, the input head position is implicit (the algorithm just reads the next bit), so the streaming algorithm itself does not store log N bits on its work tape. However, when unrolling to a circuit, the circuit must represent the entire configuration at each stage, including how much input has been consumed, to correctly compose stages. This is why the log N overhead appears in the circuit but not in the streaming algorithm's space bound. - This lemma attacks G0001 (defining the tableau encoding) by explicitly including the input head counter. It does not close G0002 (formal worst-case update time definition) or hypothesis (8). Reviewer must be of another model family.

statement_start: LEMMA (Corrected Sigma_3SAT^A stage map with self-delimiting oracle A, repairs S0044). Let M be a one-pass streaming algorithm that decides the language Sigma_3SAT^A for some oracle A. M reads input x in {0,1}^N in order. In each interval between input reads, M performs at most tau steps and at most q oracle calls to A. By MMW19 Theorem 1.2, M queries oracle A using a self-delimiting encoding so that A ignores trailing bits. Each query to A has variable length at most ell. Let ell <= poly(S) + otilde(tau). Then the stage map from (configuration at read i, input bit x_{i+1}) to configuration at read i+1 is computed by a single A-oracle circuit with the following properties: (a) Exactly tau*q oracle gates of fixed input length ell, each querying oracle A. (b) tau * poly(S) ordinary fan-in-2 gates for the computation between queries. (c) Uniform structure over all inputs x. (d) The self-delimiting encoding is implemented in the circuit: for each oracle call, the circuit takes the query string y generated by M, computes its self-delimiting encoding (length prefix + y), pads to exactly ell bits, and feeds this to the fixed ell-input oracle gate. Since A ignores trailing bits by the self-delimiting assumption, the oracle answer on the padded string equals the answer on the original query. No padding-invariance assumption on Sigma_3SAT^A is needed or used; the padding invariance is a property of the self-delimiting encoding for oracle A.
statement_end: PROOF: Identical to the proof of S0017_REPAIR, with the clarification that the oracle gates query A (not Sigma_3SAT^A). The language Sigma_3SAT^A is the language M decides; A is the oracle M queries. MMW19 Theorem 1.2 explicitly states: 'The oracle A is queried via a self-delimiting encoding... so that the oracle ignores trailing bits.' This is a property of M's query protocol to A, not a property of the Sigma_3SAT^A language. The circuit construction implements M's query protocol faithfully. QED. SCOPE: This lemma corrects S0044 by removing the incorrect padding-invariance assumption on Sigma_3SAT^A and correctly attributing the self-delimiting encoding to oracle A. It closes the per-stage size bound for the A-oracle circuit (gap G0003), same as S0017_REPAIR. It does not close G0001, G0002, or hypothesis (8). Reviewer must be of another model family.

statement_start: LEMMA (Formal worst-case update time for MMW19 streaming algorithm, closes G0002). Let M be a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm in the MMW19 model (Theorem 1.2). M has work space S(n) = O(s(n)^c) cells of O(log s(n)) bits each, and reads input x in {0,1}^N (N = 2^n) left-to-right in a single pass. For each i = 0,1,...,N-1, let T_i(x) be the number of steps M executes between reading input bit i and input bit i+1 (with i=0 meaning before reading the first bit; M starts in initial configuration). Define the worst-case update time of M as u(N) = max_{x in {0,1}^N, i in [0,N-1]} T_i(x). Then: (1) u(N) is well-defined and finite for every N (M is a deterministic algorithm with a fixed transition function). (2) The circuit construction in Lemmas S0169, S0170, S0171 uses tau = u(N) as the number of steps per interval. (3) If M runs in total time T(N) on N-bit inputs, then u(N) <= T(N) (trivially, since total time bounds per-interval time). (4) MMW19 Theorem 1.2 assumes the streaming algorithm runs in poly(S) time overall, which implies u(N) <= poly(S) = poly(s(n)^c). However, the theorem does NOT explicitly bound u(N) independently of the total runtime; the per-interval bound tau is derived from the overall poly(S) bound.
statement_end: PROOF: (1) M is a deterministic algorithm with a fixed finite transition function. For any input x and any interval i, the sequence of configurations is uniquely determined. Since M halts on every input (it decides a language), each interval has a finite number of steps. The maximum over the finite set of all 2^N inputs and N intervals exists and is finite. (2) In the circuit construction (S0170), we explicitly pad each interval to exactly tau steps. Choosing tau = u(N) guarantees that every interval fits within the padded length, and no interval exceeds tau steps. The circuit size is then O(u(N) * (S + log N)). (3) Summing T_i(x) over i=0..N-1 gives the total number of steps M takes on input x, which is at most T(N). Since each T_i(x) <= u(N), we have N * u(N) >= T(N), so u(N) >= T(N)/N. But the trivial bound u(N) <= T(N) also holds because u(N) is a maximum of terms each bounded by the sum. (4) MMW19 Theorem 1.2 states: 'The algorithm uses S(n) = O(s(n)^c) cells of O(log s(n)) bits each on its work tape... and runs in time poly(S).' The 'runs in time poly(S)' refers to the total runtime over the entire N-bit input. Since there are N = 2^n intervals, the worst-case per-interval update time u(N) could be as large as poly(S) (if all work is concentrated in one interval) or as small as poly(S)/N (if work is evenly distributed). The theorem does not assume a per-interval bound independent of N. QED. SCOPE: This lemma formalizes the worst-case update time u(N) and connects it to the circuit parameter tau. It closes G0002 by providing the explicit definition that was missing. It shows that tau = u(N) is the correct parameter, and that MMW19's poly(S) total time bound implies u(N) <= poly(S) but not necessarily u(N) <= poly(s) or u(N) <= poly(log N). The remaining open question (hypothesis 8) is whether u(N) can be bounded by poly(s) independent of N for the specific Sigma_3SAT^A algorithm. Reviewer must be of another model family.
